unlisted_practices: CMS should look closely at how the FDA implements Predetermined Change Control Plans and use similar strategies to guide coding of generalist radiology AI.
Developers, clinicians, and payors should collaboratively plan how to gather the real-world data needed to evaluate generalist radiology AI for coverage.
Coverage policies should be revamped to accommodate dynamic, adaptive AI tools such as generalist radiology AI.
The ACR and other radiology organizations should determine how best to validate generalist radiology AI to support society recommendations for coverage.

CMS and the AMA should establish an objective and transparent reimbursement framework that incentivizes adoption of high-quality, clinically impactful generalist radiology AI while ensuring fair compensation for radiologists and providers.
Payors and other stakeholders should proactively explore how generalist radiology AI payment would be structured in terms of coding, valuation, and coverage.
CMS and the AMA should develop coding for generalist radiology AI, such as a multi-task coordination code, a modality-specific code series, or modifiers building on existing radiology codes.
Valuation of generalist radiology AI should use a composite, multifaceted RVU reflecting radiologist work, task complexity, and adaptability, with higher valuation as autonomy increases.
